Heard Mr. Barun Kumar Chakrabarty, learned counsel for the appellants as well as Ms. Madhunisha Singh, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State/respondent, on IA No. 1 of 2022, which is an application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Though notice issued to the father (PW-3) of the prosecutrix is said to have been served, none has appeared on his behalf.
As per prosecution story, the appellants are alleged to have committed rape upon the prosecutrix (PW-2), a minor girl aged about 9 years and 9 months, on 25.08.2020 at 3:00 p.m. in a lonely place.
It has been argued by the Mr. Barun Kumar Chakrabarty, learned counsel for the appellants that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
There are no eye-witnesses to the incident.
There is no authentic documentary proof with regard to the age of the victim.
The case is based on circumstantial evidence and the incident is said to have taken place at 3 p.m. when there are number of people on the streets.
The witnesses in this case are interested witness being the relatives of the victim.
Mr. Chakrabarty submits that the only allegation against the appellant No. 2- Kumesh Kumar Sahu is that he assisted in commission of the crime but he himself has not committed the crime.
Thus, no offence under the POCSO Act, 2012 is made out against the appellant No. 2.
The learned trial court has convicted the appellants without there being any reliable material or evidence on record.
The appellants are in jail since 26.08.2020 and the disposal of this appeal is going to take quite long time.
Hence, their conviction and sentence may kindly be suspended and the appellants may be released on bail.

On the other hand, Ms. Madhunisha Singh, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State/respondent submits that the prosecutrix being minor on the date of incident is well established from the School Admission Register (Exhibit P-43).

The medical report of the prosecutrix (Exhibit P-19), medical report of the accused (Exhibit P-21) and the FSL report (Exhibit Omkar Sahu @ Bhagwat Sahu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166965427/
2 P-36) clearly leads to the only conclusion that the appellants have committed the offence.

sentences.text:
The learned trial Court, after appreciating the evidence on record and after examining the cross- examination of the witnesses, has rightly come to the conclusion regarding guilt of the appellants,
which is just and proper.

Considering the fact that on the date of incident, the prosecutrix was a minor aged 9 years and 9 months who has been subjected to rape by two of the accused in a brutal manner which is evident from the Exhibit P/19 i.e. the medical examination report of the prosecutrix in which the Doctor has found multiple abrasion over back, abdomen, chest and thigh area, further on her genital examination, her hymen has been found ruptured and presence of mild redness, and that the Doctor has also opined that the findings are suggestive of forceful sexual act.
Even in the statement of the prosecutrix herself, she has clearly deposed and identified the appellants.

So far as the involvement of appellant No. 2 in this case is concerned, the appellant No. 2 alongwith appellant No. 1 have been found guilty of the offence under Section 376 (D, B) of the IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act,
2012, we deem it appropriate to reject the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail,
at this stage.
Accordingly, IA No. 1/2022 stand disposed of.
Let this case be listed for final hearing.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (N.K.Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
